How much a self-selected threshold inflates the reported level

Source: R/paired.R
tss_inflation.Rd

The true skill statistic (TSS) is overestimated when the threshold is chosen to maximise TSS on the same held-out observations used to report the score. The fewer presences there are in the held-out data, the more TSS tends to overestimate population skill. tss_inflation() estimates the TSS that a given sampling design would report for a known population skill. implied_skill() reverses this calculation: given a reported TSS, it estimates the population skill that would yield that score on average under the same sampling design and assumed prediction distribution. This simulation-based matching follows the principle of indirect inference (Gouriéroux et al., 1993).

Usage

tss_inflation(y, folds, skill = c(0.6, 0.7, 0.9), replicates = 200L, seed = 1L)

Arguments

y

The response: a matrix or data frame of units by variables, with unit identifiers in the row names or in a leading character or factor column.

folds

A fold map from fold_map(), or any named integer vector of the same shape.

skill

Population skill values to simulate.

replicates

Replicates per value.

seed

Random seed.

Value

A data frame with one row per skill value: the skill, the mean level read back, the inflation, and its interval across replicates.

Details

Predictions are simulated for each value of skill as normal scores of equal variance, at the cell sizes and presence counts of the response and fold map supplied. The TSS is read at its best threshold exactly as grain_ladder() reports it, and the mean reading minus skill is the inflation.

The inflation is an expectation. A level read on one design is optimistic on average, not a bound every reading sits above: a single level can fall below the population skill. Predictions distributed otherwise inflate by a different amount at the same skill, which is also why a paired difference paired_contrast() takes is not free of it.

Examples

set.seed(1)
y <- matrix(rbinom(1200, 1, 0.15), nrow = 200,
            dimnames = list(sprintf("p%03d", 1:200), paste0("sp", 1:6)))
tss_inflation(y, fold_map(y, v = 5), skill = c(0.6, 0.9), replicates = 40)
